newsitem.title: INDIA: Late demand boosts Indian call to 8.0 pct at close.
newsitem.headline: Late demand boosts Indian call to 8.0 pct at close.

text.p: A late surge in demand from a few banks boosted Indian call money rates to eight percent at close of trade on Wednesday, dealers said.
They said demand from some banks with uncovered positions led to an unexpected rise in call money rates after most of the day's deals were done between six percent and 6.75 percent.

"The bulk of the deals is normally done in the first half hour after start of trade," said a dealer. "Rates were in the 6.0-6.75 band at that time. Subsequently it is only some last-minute covering by a few banks."
Dealers said some afternoon deals were done at eight percent with a stray deal at 8.25 percent.
The government securities market was largely inactive with market players interested in selling, dealers said. Prices fell on selling pressure, they said.
"It was largely one-way with most players looking only to sell," said a dealer.

The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock traded on Wednesday at 102.87 rupees against its last traded price of 103.04 while the 13.50 percent 1998 stock dropped to 103.08 from 103.27, dealers said.
Treasury bills maturing in May yielded eight percent against last yield of 7.85, they said.
Dealers said there were no trades in commercial paper or certificates of deposit.
